entries.event: FOMC Minutes of the 28–29 July 2026 meeting
entries.consensus: No numeric consensus. Market benchmark is ~25–31% implied probability of a 25bp hike at the 15–16 Sep meeting, down from ~60% on 1 Aug and a ~82% late-July peak. For this entry read 'above consensus' as 'more hawkish than that pricing implies'.
entries.actual: Minutes of the 28-29 July meeting released 19 Aug: many participants judged further tightening could become necessary if inflation fails to moderate; the record detailed the three dissents for an immediate hike. September 25bp hike probability afterwards sat at roughly 31-32% (Kalshi 32c), versus the ~25-31% benchmark, and the dollar fell to a three-month low that week.
entries.note: The content was widely characterised as hawkish (ING: 'Fed minutes lean hawkish, but we don't expect a hike'), which is directionally consistent with the call, but the benchmark was explicitly pricing-based and pricing barely moved - prediction-market commentary described the minutes as supporting the existing ~31% probability. Since the hawkishness was already discounted and the dollar weakened on the Treasury buyback story instead, the lean cannot honestly be scored a hit.

entries.event: President Trump speaks (30 minutes after the FOMC minutes)
entries.consensus: No consensus; unscripted headline risk. Topic set most likely centres on the Canada tariff pause, Iran/Hormuz, and possibly monetary policy.
entries.actual: Trump hosted cryptocurrency and finance leaders in the Roosevelt Room, with remarks touching on digital assets, prediction markets, North Korea and interest rates; separately he said the US is not in talks with Iran. No single FX-defining headline emerged from the event itself.
entries.note: Lean was 'no clear lean', which resolves unclear by construction. The topic set skewed to crypto and foreign policy rather than the Canada tariff pause anticipated in the note.

entries.event: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, August 2026
entries.actual: 47.4 in August versus a 24.1 consensus (Haver cites expectations of 25.0), up from 41.4 in July and a five-year high; the ISM-adjusted index eased to 57.5 from 58.1.
entries.note: Large beat on the side the lean called, though the call was held at low confidence and the magnitude was far beyond anything the evidence supported.

entries.event: US initial jobless claims, week ending 15 August 2026
entries.actual: 206K for the week ending 15 August versus a 210K consensus; prior week revised up to 212K from 209K; continuing claims 1.799mn.
entries.note: Printed below consensus as the lean called, consistent with the low-layoff pattern after July's 189K near-60-year low. The 4-week average still rose to 204K.

entries.event: UK retail sales volumes m/m, July 2026 (ONS)
entries.actual: ONS: retail sales volumes fell 0.5% m/m in July 2026, exactly matching the -0.5% consensus; total spend including online fell 0.6% m/m with online sales values down 3.9%, while supermarkets and alcoholic drinks benefited from hot weather.
entries.note: Printed exactly on consensus, so the 'above consensus' lean neither hit nor missed. The hot-weather food and drink support the note relied on was present but offset by a sharp online drop.

entries.event: HCOB France flash manufacturing PMI, August 2026
entries.actual: HCOB France flash manufacturing PMI 51.5 in August versus a 50.0-50.1 consensus, up from 49.8 in July and back into expansion; the composite nonetheless fell to 48.8 from 49.4 on service-sector weakness.
entries.note: Clear miss - the lean called below consensus and manufacturing beat by about 1.4pts. Notably the composite did weaken, so the underlying French growth concern was right but expressed in the wrong sub-index.

entries.event: US core PCE price index m/m, July 2026 (BEA, released with the Q2 second estimate)
entries.consensus: 0.2% m/m (previous 0.1%); core y/y expected to ease to about 3.2% from 3.3%
entries.actual: Core PCE +0.2% m/m (about +0.25% unrounded per Employ America), core y/y 3.3%, unchanged from June; headline +0.2% m/m and 3.7% y/y
entries.note: Lean was 'in line' and core landed exactly on consensus on both m/m and y/y (CNBC/Yahoo: both readings as expected). The caveat: our brief expected core y/y to ease to about 3.2%; it held at 3.3%, and the headline surprised 0.1pp high on energy. Employ America flagged the m/m strength as concentrated in portfolio management fees, healthcare and airfares.

entries.event: US Q2 2026 GDP, second estimate (BEA), with corporate profits
entries.consensus: 1.5% q/q annualised, unrevised from the 30 July advance estimate

entries.event: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (symposium 27-29 Aug, theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy')
entries.consensus: No numeric consensus. The benchmark is that a neutral, 'big picture' address is expected - roughly 69% of fund managers surveyed by BofA look for a neutral tone. Read 'above consensus' as hawkish relative to that, 'below consensus' as dovish.
entries.actual: Hawkish keynote. Warsh said inflation's 'underlying trends' had not improved and that summer's better readings 'do not' settle the matter, called price stability 'not self-executing' and inflation the predominant focus, praised real-activity strength and downplayed labour-market risk; September hike odds rose to roughly a coin flip from about a third
entries.note: Our lean was 'no clear lean' at low confidence, so by construction this is unscored. Honest read: the neutral-tone benchmark (roughly 69% of BofA-surveyed managers) was wrong-footed and we did not call the hawkish direction. Bond-market reaction was described as muted despite the repricing.

entries.event: BLS preliminary estimate of the 2026 annual benchmark revision to establishment-survey employment (March 2026 level), published with Q1 2026 QCEW
entries.consensus: No published consensus; the anchor is last year's record -911K preliminary revision for March 2025. Read 'above consensus' as a materially smaller downward revision than that anchor, 'below consensus' as another very large downward revision.
entries.actual: -79,000 (-0.1%) for the March 2026 benchmark level, concentrated in retail and several other major sectors
entries.note: Lean was 'above consensus', i.e. a materially smaller downward revision than the -911K March 2025 anchor. -79K is an order of magnitude smaller and among the mildest preliminary revisions on record; Bloomberg reported the median economist projection looked for a larger markdown.

entries.event: Treasury Secretary Bessent press conference, Treasury Department, 14:00 ET / 18:00 GMT
entries.consensus: No numeric consensus. Billed as the unveiling of new Iran sanctions after Bessent's FT op-ed warning of an 'economic D-Day'; buyback and debt-management questions are near-certain.
entries.actual: Bessent unveiled 'Operation Economic Outcast', a sustained sanctions campaign against Iran and its 'enablers', and said on secondary targets that 'no one is above the reach of U.S. sanctions'; Iran said it was 'fully prepared'
entries.note: Lean was 'no clear lean' at low confidence; no numeric benchmark existed. The event delivered the pre-trailed sanctions escalation rather than a debt-management surprise, and energy prices remain the transmission channel into G4 inflation prints.

entries.event: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index, August 2026
entries.actual: 89.4 in August versus 90.2-90.3 expected; July revised down to 90.2 from 90.8; Expectations 68.2 from 74.0, Present Situation 121.2 from 114.4
entries.note: Lean was 'below consensus' and the index printed 0.8-0.9pt below, a seven-month low, with the miss driven entirely by the Expectations component (labour-market and business-conditions pessimism, elevated mentions of energy prices and geopolitics). Market impact was negligible, as expected for this series.

BoE Governor Andrew Bailey keynote, LSE TRIUM Anniversary Conference, London (09:50 BST / 08:50 GMT, 4 Sep)
entries.consensus: No numeric consensus. Benchmark is a broad, structural keynote with no fresh near-term policy signal, consistent with Bailey's recent practice. Read 'above consensus' as hawkish relative to that (opening the door to a 17 Sept hike), 'below consensus' as dovish.
